I'm relatively unhelpful as most of my experience is 5-10 years old and I'm just getting started building again. I'm going to assume you are getting good general info from other sources and sick with Linux specific.

Nvidia cards have a history of not playing nice with Ubuntu. I have had to reinstall Ubuntu after a bad driver update gave me a black screen of death and refused to startup. However, newer cards (one to two years old and newer) apparently aren't having as many problems. I'd make sure you check driver support-both vendor and Linux community-for any video cards you consider.

Your list looks alright to me, but if you care about noise at all I'd add a CPU cooler to that, for example a Cooler Master Hyper 212 Plus would be a decent choice. Also that case might not be the quietest, but if that's not so important to you you can pick pretty much any case you like as long as the motherboard and the GPU will fit.

For motherboard you could probably just pick the cheapest one with the right socket if you're not going to overclock. As far as I know there's not much difference in reliability between the different brands.

For PSU you want something with a good score at JonnyGURU. Looking at the brand is not enough since many good brands have also made crap. (I didn't find a review for the particular PSU one you listed.)

For GNU/Linux support H-node is a good source, although most desktop hardware will work fine with proprietary drivers. Nvidia has generally had better Linux support than AMD in the past, I don't know if the situation has changed.

If you are doing most of your gaming on windows, check out an AMD card. You can probably get more bang for your buck than the 970, and the Linux drivers are fine, unless you plan to game primarily on gaming, in which case stick with Nvidia. Otherwise, your build looks good.

For motherboards, Gigabyte, Asus, and Asrock have a good reputation. I have used Asrock and Asus, and I preferred the Asus (the asrock was a bit fidgety with recognizing my keyboard during boot). EVGA motherboards are also great, but quite expensive.

For RAM, its really not a big deal, since a RAM failure will rarely take other components with it. Kingston is my favorite, but Gskill also has some nice products as well. Crucial is decent too.

For hard drives, Hitachi or WD is the way to go. Avoid Segates if at all possible. I have no strong feelings regarding Toshiba. For SSDs, Samsung and Intel are the top tier brands. Crucial is pretty solid too. Kingston has some good reliable SSDs for good prices, but they are not as performant as the other brands.

For cases, Fractal Design is the best hands down, at least for mind and full ATX cases. NZXT is solid all round, especially the NZXT source 210 pro, which is my favorite for builds where budget is a concern. Silverstone also has some worthwhile offerings in the ITX form factor department.

For PSUs, Seasonic is by far the best. EVGA is great also. Higher end XFX PSUs are actually rebranded Seasonics. Corsair is decent.

When it comes to Linux compatibility, the only major concern is your video card. Nvidia has okay proprietary drivers, and sub par open source drivers. AMD has decent open source drivers, and crappy proprietary drivers. Intel has the best drivers by far, but Intel integrated graphics are obviously not ideal for gaming. Ultimately, the Linux driver situation is not ideal, but Nvidia is generally better for gaming, if you are okay with closed source drivers. Pretty much everything else should "just work". These days that includes most wifi adapters too!
